cases.prompt: Sketch the layout and flow for a two-step checkout screen.
cases.rationale: Layout and flow with no real colour, type or spacing named. wireframe-design's own text claims exactly this; high-fidelity-ui-design's text disclaims it as a separate later round.

cases.prompt: Breadboard the onboarding flow — what places exist and what connects them?
cases.rationale: "Breadboard" is a term only wireframe-design claims. Nothing is being implemented, so a styling capability firing here would be a genuine over-reach.

cases.prompt: Give me two low-fidelity layout options for a settings page so we can pick one.
cases.rationale: "Low-fidelity" and options-comparison are both named in wireframe-design's text. The explicit fidelity marker makes this the clearest case in the set.

cases.prompt: Grey-box the regions of an analytics dashboard before we argue about colour.
cases.rationale: Deliberately defers colour. If either colour-bearing skill fires on a prompt that rules colour out in words, the boundary is not holding.

cases.prompt: Define the semantic colour tokens for our app, including dark mode.
cases.rationale: Token design is high-fidelity-ui-design's; the styling skill also names tokens because it implements them, so its appearance is legitimate rather than spurious.

cases.prompt: Check whether our button colours meet WCAG contrast in both themes.
cases.rationale: Real colour and a WCAG target: precisely what the wireframe skill says it does not cover.

cases.prompt: Design a type scale and decide the body text size for readability.
cases.rationale: Typography as the subject rather than as a placeholder — the fidelity line wireframe-design draws against itself.

cases.prompt: What states does a primary button need — hover, disabled, loading, error?
cases.rationale: Complete interaction-state sets are high-fidelity-ui-design's. Both React skills name states too, so either appearing is defensible.

cases.prompt: Are our tap targets big enough on mobile, and is the focus ring visible?
cases.rationale: Touch-target sizing and visible focus are named in high-fidelity-ui-design's text; react-component-styling names pointer-sized targets as an implementation concern.

cases.prompt: Write the CSS Module for a Card component.
cases.rationale: Naming the concrete file type should route unambiguously to the styling implementation skill.

cases.prompt: Convert this React Native StyleSheet.create over to Unistyles with variants.
cases.rationale: A named library and a mechanical conversion. Neither design skill has anything to contribute, so either firing is a spurious trigger.

cases.prompt: This sidebar breaks below 600px — container query or media query?
cases.rationale: Container-driven responsiveness is named directly in react-component-styling's discovery text.

cases.prompt: Should this component take a className prop, and how do I merge it?
cases.rationale: The styling-prop merge contract is react-component-styling's. The component skill also names the props spread, so it is a legitimate co-selection.

cases.prompt: What order should the properties go in inside this stylesheet?
cases.rationale: Style property order is a mechanic only the styling skill claims — a narrow probe of whether the design skills over-trigger on the word 'style'.

cases.prompt: Make this animated accordion respect prefers-reduced-motion.
cases.rationale: Both name reduced motion — the styling skill as an adaptive rule, the design skill as preference-aware motion. Implementation is asked for, so the styling skill must appear.

cases.prompt: Review this component for both its visual hierarchy and how its CSS is organised.
cases.rationale: Deliberately contested: it asks two questions that two skills own separately. The coverage line is the point — a split distribution here is healthy, and neither skill should read as a miss.

cases.prompt: The wireframe is settled — now pick the real colours and spacing for it.
cases.rationale: Names the wireframe as finished context. Tests whether the word 'wireframe' pulls the wrong skill in even when the ask has moved past it.

cases.prompt: Add a database migration that backfills the orders table.
cases.rationale: No UI surface at all. A control: if any design skill fires here, its discovery text is far too broad.

cases.prompt: This Playwright test is flaky — fix the waiting.
cases.rationale: A control with a positive expectation attached: end-to-end-testing names Playwright and flakiness explicitly, so this also checks the fixture can detect a plain hit outside the pilot trio.

cases.prompt: Write the commit message for this change.
cases.rationale: A second outside-the-trio control. conventional-commits claims this in as many words, so a miss here would point at the harness rather than at the trio.

cases.prompt: Our React Native app's Amplitude device ID resets on every launch. What's wrong?
cases.rationale: The AsyncStorage identity slot is a pure Amplitude mechanism, named in amplitude-instrumentation's text. software-instrumentation is deliberately vendor-neutral and owns no SDK's storage behaviour, so its appearance would mean the vendor boundary is not holding.

cases.prompt: Set up Amplitude Session Replay without recording every single session.
cases.rationale: The sharpest vendor-versus-vendor collision in the set: Amplitude and Sentry both ship a product called Session Replay, both document a sample rate, and both skills name masking. The prompt names Amplitude, so the other vendor firing here is a genuine mis-route rather than a defensible co-selection — and this is the one case that would catch two vendor skills competing for a shared product noun.

cases.prompt: Should this Amplitude user property use set or setOnce?
cases.rationale: The Identify operator set is Amplitude's API. A narrow probe of whether an Amplitude-named API question pulls the vendor-neutral skill in unnecessarily.

cases.prompt: What should we name this event so it survives a redesign, and where should the tracking call go?
cases.rationale: The reverse direction. Naming and call-site placement are exactly what software-instrumentation's product-event reference claims and what amplitude-instrumentation explicitly disclaims. If the vendor skill fires on an unnamed vendor, its discovery text is too broad.

cases.prompt: Make sure no analytics fires before the user accepts cookies.
cases.rationale: Consent gating is covered by both, but no vendor is named. The vendor-specific skill firing here would mean it is competing for every analytics prompt rather than Amplitude ones — that half passed, at amplitude-instrumentation 0/5. software-instrumentation measured 0/5 and is a standing MISS: its when_to_use lists both "analytics" and "consent gating" as literal triggers, yet natural phrasing about accepting cookies surfaces neither skill. Left deliberately red rather than relabelled, because it is a real discoverability gap in that skill and this evaluation reports rather than gates. Tracked separately; do not silence this case without fixing the text it measures.

cases.prompt: We use Amplitude — name this checkout event and wire up the track call.
cases.rationale: Deliberately contested: naming belongs to software-instrumentation, the Amplitude track mechanism to amplitude-instrumentation. Originally labelled with both as mustInclude; the first real run measured amplitude-instrumentation 5/5 and software-instrumentation 0/5 at coverage 5/5, so nothing was lost and the label was the error rather than the behaviour. Demoted to mayInclude because the only other remedy — widening software-instrumentation until it fires on a prompt that names a vendor — would break the three amp-* cases that require it absent. A one-turn measurement picking the more specific skill on an explicitly vendor-named prompt is legitimate either way.

cases.prompt: Our production stack traces come through minified even though the Sentry build plugin runs on every deploy. What should I check?
cases.rationale: A vendor-specific wiring failure — source maps, release/dist matching, the bundler wrapper. sentry-instrumentation's when_to_use names 'source maps' and 'an unsymbolicated stack trace' in as many words. software-instrumentation is legitimately adjacent because it owns error tracking generally, but owns none of these mechanics, so its appearance is neither required nor wrong.

cases.prompt: Should this recoverable retry be logged at warn or info, and where should the catch live?
cases.rationale: The counterpart to sentry-minified-traces, and the direction that matters: log-level choice and catch placement are vendor-neutral, named in software-instrumentation's own text, and sentry-instrumentation explicitly hands them back ('For log levels, catch placement, and which failures are worth capturing at all, use a software instrumentation capability instead'). A spurious selection here means the vendor skill's triggers are too broad — the collision this pair exists to detect.
